hero.alt: Cream title card reading How Many Rakat in Wudu?

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 164 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Uthman's wudu demonstration with washing three times; two rak'ahs without distraction and forgiveness of past sins.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 226a on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Uthman's narration: two rak'ahs after wudu without distracted thoughts; previous sins expiated.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 234a on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Uqbah ibn Amir: wudu done well then two rak'ahs with heart and face; Paradise guaranteed.

sources.title: Sunan Abi Dawud 906 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Same meaning as Muslim 234a; graded sahih by al-Albani.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1149 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Bilal praying after every purification as much as was written for him, with no number given.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Voluntary prayers
sources.supports: Prayer after wudu is voluntary; Bilal's two rak'a practice known as the two rak'as of wudu.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Disliked prayer times
sources.supports: Prayers with a prior reason, including the two rak'as after ablution, permitted at disliked times; istikhara contrast.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 831 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Three forbidden times: sunrise, midday height of the sun, and sunset.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 586 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: No prayer after the morning prayer until sunrise or after Asr until sunset.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Which salahs can't be performed at makrooh times?
sources.supports: Makruh to pray any nafl after the Fajr and Asr prayers.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Tahiyatul Masjid at the time of Zawaal
sources.supports: Hanafi scholars hold the greeting prayer prohibitively disliked in the restricted times.

review.notes: Every claim was checked against captured text. No checked source names the prayer after wudu in a Hanafi ruling, so the article states that the application to it comes from the words any nafl. Dar al-Ifta's exception is reported as its explanation and not as consensus.

claim_checks.claim: Whoever makes wudu like this and prays two rak'ahs without distraction has past sins forgiven.
claim_checks.explanation: The captured narration from Humran about Uthman says this in the Prophet's words.

claim_checks.claim: Any Muslim who makes wudu well then prays two rak'ahs with heart and face set on them is guaranteed Paradise.
claim_checks.explanation: The captured narration from Uqbah ibn Amir states this.

claim_checks.claim: Bilal prayed after every purification as much as was written for him.
claim_checks.explanation: The text gives no number, as the article notes.

claim_checks.claim: The prayer after wudu is voluntary and is known as the two rak'as of wudu.
claim_checks.explanation: The section The prayer after wudu uses this description.

claim_checks.claim: Dar al-Ifta lists the two rak'as after ablution among prayers allowed at disliked times, unlike istikhara.
claim_checks.explanation: The fatwa names both and gives the prior-reason distinction.

claim_checks.claim: It is makruh to pray any nafl after the Fajr prayer and after the Asr prayer.
claim_checks.explanation: Items two and three of the answer state this.

claim_checks.claim: The greeting of the mosque is not allowed during times when salah is not permitted.
claim_checks.explanation: The conclusion says so, attributing the dislike to Hanafi scholars.

claim_checks.claim: Three restricted times at sunrise, midday and sunset.
claim_checks.explanation: The narration from Uqbah lists these three.

claim_checks.claim: No prayer after the morning prayer until sunrise or after Asr until sunset.
claim_checks.explanation: The narration from Abu Said al-Khudri says this.
